why: Commits 1 and 3 are fully named and checked (a scan for unoptimized, a 404 on /_next/image, a 20 KB test on the folder, header checks), but commit 2 sets storage lifetimes that cannot be taken back for files already stored, and its scan test only checks that a cacheControl or a 'year'/'short' word is present, not which value goes where. A year on the replicator's rewritten previews or on a private digital file or CSV, or '0' on a public video, would pass every check.
harm_if_wrong: A file written again under the same path stays stale for a year in browsers and the CDN, or a private file (a paid digital download, an import CSV) is marked cacheable, and nothing fails.
make_it_cheaper: Make file-lifetimes.scan.test.ts assert the exact value per file (a table: video-upload, media-compress, product-media-tools, field-file-upload, theme-shots, replicate-assets -> year; product-editor and the four import flows -> "0"; replicate-store -> "short"), and state field-file-upload's bucket outright, so commit 2 needs no read of the diff.
brief_problems: field-file-upload.ts leaves the bucket choice to the executor, yet its own StartFieldFile doc comment already says 'a signed upload to the public bucket': the brief could name the year outright.
The scan test's tag rule ('from <Image to the first />') also matches tags like <ImageSomething in a file that imports next/image; the test should match only `<Image` followed by whitespace.
